data:
Status: planned, wave 4; repositories not created yet, names provisional (expr, poly, groebner, integrate, series, linalg).
The core is Mathematica’s symbolic core in Go: an expression DAG with canonical forms, polynomial arithmetic over Z, Q and F_p, GCD and factorisation, differentiation, LaTeX output, then Gröbner bases, integration, series and limits (PLAN.md items 18 and 21, wave 4).
No code exists yet: nothing on this page is released, measured or tested. It says what the library is planned to provide and how it will be checked. The wave and the order are in PLAN.md; the state of each item in STATUS.md.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be:
Reference tools are run as oracles, driven from Go by exec with JSON on a pipe; the unit suite must pass with no oracle installed.
Oracle How SymPy uv run --with sympy; compare by simplify(a-b)==0 or numeric spot checks, not strings python-flint uv run --with python-flint; fmpz_poly.factor(), fmpz_mpoly PARI/GP, Maxima, FriCAS exec with JSON or text on a pipe; FriCAS to verify Risch results Rubi suite converted to JSON of (integrand, variable, optimal antiderivative); checked by differentiation What “correct” means:
Area Criterion Polynomials, exact linear algebra exact equality after canonical form Factorisation product equals the input and every factor is irreducible per the oracle Gröbner the reduced basis is unique for a given order: exact equality with Singular, Giac or Sage output Integration derivative of the result minus the integrand simplifies to 0; Rubi grade histogram (A, B, C, F) Limits, series, solve exact equality of normal forms, or numeric spot checks at random points with N-digit arithmetic Output LaTeX compiles and typesets through go-tex; round trip through a parser gives the same tree
data.reference-implementations#Reference impl: Implementation Licence and use SymPy (Python) BSD-3 text; port permitted file by file after reading the appended notices; reference for Gruntz, Risch, solve, simplify FriCAS (Common Lisp) BSD-3-Clause; port permitted; the most complete Risch implementation Rubi (Mathematica rules and tests) MIT; rules and the 72,000-problem suite are reusable data FLINT, PARI/GP, Maxima, Giac, Sage LGPL or GPL: oracles only, never copied

data.risks-and-open-questions#Risks and open: A CAS comparable to Mathematica is a decades-long target; Rubi, Risch, Gröbner and polynomial factorisation are each a project. Two correct antiderivatives can differ by a constant or a form, so the oracle comparison is by differentiation. GC pressure on many small big.Int is a risk for polynomial arithmetic; word-sized coefficient fast paths for F_p come first. GPL and LGPL systems are oracles only; SymPy, SymEngine and Reduce need their LICENSE files read before any port.
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: Expression DAG hash-consed, canonical forms, diff, expand, LaTeX output through go-tex Polynomials over Z, Q and F_p, rational functions; word-sized uint64 fast paths for F_p GCD modular GCD (Brown) with CRT, heuristic GCD for small cases, sparse Zippel for multivariate Factorisation over F_p: square-free, distinct-degree, equal-degree (Cantor-Zassenhaus); over Z: factor mod p, Hensel lifting, recombination by LLL (van Hoeij) Gröbner bases Buchberger with criteria, then F4 modulo p and lifting; polynomial-system solving through lex order (FGLM), triangular sets and resultants Integration rational (Hermite reduction, Lazard-Rioboo-Trager), the Risch algorithm for elementary functions, Risch-Norman, and a rule-based engine importing Rubi’s rules Series and limits truncated power series with Newton iteration; Gruntz’s algorithm for limits Exact linear algebra Bareiss fraction-free elimination, multi-modular with CRT, Dixon p-adic lifting

Status: planned, wave 4, after the core; repositories not created yet, names provisional (codegen, algnum, ode, pde, triangular, diffalg, stats, group, tensor).
What Maple offers beyond Mathematica’s core, as a delta over it (PLAN.md items 19 to 21, wave 4). Maple is proprietary and is never run as an oracle: free tools are, and the expected values are frozen into test data by a Go generator that records the tool and its version.
No code exists yet: nothing on this page is released, measured or tested. It says what the library is planned to provide and how it will be checked. The wave and the order are in PLAN.md; the state of each item in STATUS.md.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be:
Reference tools are run as oracles, driven from Go by exec with JSON on a pipe; the unit suite must pass with no oracle installed.
Oracle How ODE and PDE SymPy dsolve, classify_ode, checkodesol; FriCAS for Kovacic; correctness by substituting the solution into the equation Algebraic numbers PARI/GP (nffactor, polredabs), python-flint Triangular sets msolve, Singular, Sage (oracle only); checked by radical membership and numerical solving Groups GAP, SymPy combinatorics; exact group order and conjugacy-class sizes Code generation SymPy cse, ccode, fortran_code; go build the output and compare with the interpreter What “correct” means:
Area Criterion ODE and PDE residual after substitution is zero, or below 1e-12 relative at 100 random points; the solution is general; wrong answers must be 0 Algebraic numbers exact equality after canonical form; norm and minimal polynomial equal PARI’s Triangular decomposition union of the zero sets equals the input variety Code generation generated Go compiles, vet is clean, equals the interpreter within a stated ULP bound Groups exact: order, orbit sizes, class counts

data.risks-and-open-questions#Risks and open: ODE solving is heuristic and open-ended; Kovacic is the only complete piece. A verifier-first design and a time limit per ODE control the cost. CAD and triangular decomposition are doubly exponential in the worst case; word-size polynomial arithmetic over Z/p comes first. The Maple help pages describe interfaces, rarely algorithms: attributions to Maple are inferences and flagged as such in the bibliography. Not planned: Mathematica’s curated data (Entity, CountryData), the Maple .mw document round trip, and MapleSim’s proprietary component libraries.
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: codegen expressions to Go source with common-subexpression elimination on the hash-consed DAG, an optional Horner scheme, a fusion policy for floating point, a pluggable target interface; C and Fortran emitters as test oracles only algnum algebraic numbers (RootOf, evala-style): minimal polynomials, dynamic evaluation when the polynomial is reducible, norm, trace, GCD and factorisation over number fields ode classification, integrating factors, Lie symmetry heuristics, Kovacic’s algorithm, hypergeometric reductions; a checkodesol-style verifier first, so a wrong solution is impossible pde heuristic separation, characteristic strips, travelling waves, splitting into cases triangular regular chains and triangular decomposition, then cylindrical algebraic decomposition by triangular decomposition diffalg rankings, Ritt reduction, Rosenfeld-Groebner differential elimination stats symbolic random variables: PDF, CDF, MGF and moments from distribution definitions group permutation groups by Schreier-Sims, conjugacy classes, Cayley tables, finitely presented groups tensor abstract-index tensors with Butler-Portugal canonicalisation, curvature tensors, noncommutative algebra, Lie algebras
